The Psalmist, mourning God's absence and the triumph of his enemies, prays for relief before he is totally destroyed, and is encouraged to hope his trust will not be in vain.</title> <div sID="gen8459" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5573"/>1. The forms of expression and figure here used are frequent (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.9.12">Psa 9:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.9.18">18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.10.11">10:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.10.12">12</reference>).<div eID="gen8459" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8460" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">How long ... for ever--</hi>Shall it be for ever? <div eID="gen8460" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: PSALM 13 Psa 13:1-6 . On title, see Introduction. The Psalmist, mourning God's absence and the triumph of his enemies, prays for relief before he is totally destroyed, and is encouraged to hope his trust will not be in vain. 1. The forms of expression and figure here used are frequent (compare Psa 9:12 , 18 ; 10:11 , 12 ). How long ... for ever-- Shall it be for ever?

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5576"/><div sID="gen8463" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5576"/><hi type="bold">4. rejoice--</hi>literally, "shout as in triumph."<div eID="gen8463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8464" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I am moved--</hi>cast down from a firm position (<reference osisRef="Ps.10.6">Psa 10:6</reference>). <div eID="gen8464" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 4. rejoice-- literally, "shout as in triumph." I am moved-- cast down from a firm position ( Psa 10:6 ).
